title: 1957 AHSME Problem 31
statement: A regular octagon is to be formed by cutting equal isosceles right triangles from the corners of a square. If the square has sides of one unit, the leg of each of the triangles has length:

solutions.text:
Let \(x\) be a leg of each corner triangle. The horizontal and vertical octagon sides have length \(1-2x,\) while the four slanted sides have length \(x\sqrt2.\) Thus \[ 1-2x=x\sqrt2, \] so \[ x=\frac1{2+\sqrt2}=\frac{2-\sqrt2}{2}. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: If each cut-off leg is \(x,\) an uncut horizontal octagon side has length \(1-2x\)
A slanted octagon side is the hypotenuse \(x\sqrt2\), and regularity makes these equal
